title: Outpaint leaves a seam on bright edges - the harmonizer counts black-blended pixels as original
description: Found in MPI-918 Phase 4 (2026-10-01), ANY model, not a cloud issue. Outpaint node 687 (Mickmumpitz HarmonizeBoundary) bilinear-resizes the black-padded plate (553) to the decode's size, so the original's edge column is blended with the black bars yet still counts as known (m<0.5). The correction is pulled down by about pixel value/16, leaving a LEVEL step at the border: +3..+8 RGB on a bright sky (beach scene, grow left+right to 16:9), vs -0.5..-1.7 on MPI-900's dark wall photo. Proof (engine python, real node classes, live inputs of the cloud run): the step is unchanged when the fill is shifted 0..+24 RGB, and growing the harmonizer's hole mask by 4 px cuts it to about +-2. Fix: GrowMask on 553[1] feeding 687.inpaint_mask ONLY (686's paste mask unchanged), edited in comfy_workflows/raw/flow_outpaint.json + sync-raw-workflows.mjs. Expand must cover 1/scale of the 1 MP resize (8 covers sources up to ~10K wide, 16 up to ~21K) and GrowMask dilates one CPU pass per pixel: time it on a 16K plate. Then re-measure the seam and re-run the B1 smoke. Script: MPI-918 session scratchpad harm_proof.py, pattern in MPI-900 validation.md.
